column1: This chapter has examined a number of issues related to financial markets and monetary policy, including the question of price level determinacy with interest rate pegs, the role of the term structure of interest rates, and imperfect information in credit markets. The economics of imperfect information provides numerous insights into the structure of credit markets. Credit market imperfections commonly lead to situations in which the lender’s expected profits are not monotonic in the interest rate charged on a loan; expected profits initially rise with the loan rate but can then reach a maximum before declining. Thus, equilibrium may be characterized by credit rationing: excess demand fails to induce lenders to raise the loan rate because doing so lowers their expected profits. Perhaps more important, balance sheets matter. Variations in borrowers’ net worth a¤ect their ability to gain credit. A recession that lowers cash flows or a decline in asset prices that lowers net worth will reduce credit availability and increase the wedge between the costs of external and internal finance. The resulting impact on aggregate demand can generate a financial accelerator e¤ect.
